tiktoks.title: The Park Where Your Lunch Arrives by Drone

location.name: Shenzhen Central Park 深圳中心公园, Futian District

references.title: Shenzhen Bay Park drone delivery route (city government)
Which parks have landings, hours and payment for visitors

tiktoks.script:
## What I found

Meituan runs the network. You order in the Meituan app, a yellow-and-black drone descends onto a kiosk about the size of a vending machine, the top opens, the box drops in, and you scan a code to unlock it.

**Best spot to film — Shenzhen Central Park 深圳中心公园 (Futian).** Largest SkyPort installation, landings are visible, staff on site.

**Alternative — Shenzhen Bay Park 深圳湾公园 (Nanshan),** Zone A at North Bay Harbor, one of the main entrances. That route flies from Coastal City mall about 2km away.

Other confirmed parks: Lianhua Hill (Futian), Shenzhen Bay Coastal Ecological Park (Nanshan), North Railway Station Central Park (Longhua), Longcheng Park (Longgang), Cuihu Cultural & Sports Park (Luohu).

## Practical

- Roughly 10:00–21:00
- No drone surcharge — standard Meituan delivery fee (¥3–9) plus the food
- Grounded in heavy rain, strong wind or typhoon
- Kiosks are fenced. Stay behind the line, don't stand under the landing pad
- Meituan app is Chinese-only; pay through Alipay or WeChat Pay with an international card

## Open questions

- Which kiosk actually gets the most landings at lunchtime
- Whether staff mind a tripod, and how long you can loiter
- Whether the landing is long enough to carry a shot on its own, or whether the video is really order → wait → reveal

tiktoks.title: Shenzhen's Most Famous Cyberpunk View

location.name: One Avenue 卓悦中心, Futian CBD

references.title: Cyberpunk view from Gangxia North Exit 4

tiktoks.script:
## Getting there

Out of **Gangxia North Station 岗厦北站, Exit 4**, then the street-level canyon toward One Avenue 卓悦中心, with Civic Center and the Futian CBD towers around you.

The junction in the photo reads 金田路 / 深南大道 — One Avenue's official address is the Shennan / Jintian Road interchange, so that lines up.

## What I found

**Gangxia North is worth filming on the way through.** The station itself is the "Eye of Shenzhen": a spiral atrium with circular glass windows and a glass tunnel, and there's a marked spot on the platform telling you where to stand for the shot. Cyberpunk underground, cyberpunk at street level — two looks, one stop.

**Careful with the station name.** One Avenue's own directions send you from *Gangxia* Exit B (~5 min), which is a different station from *Gangxia North*. Worth knowing if Exit 4 doesn't put you where you expect.

## Open questions

- Blue hour or full dark — the reel and the photo are both night
- Whether the atrium is its own video or the cold open for this one
- How busy the pavement is at the framing you want, and whether a tripod is realistic there

tiktoks.title: The Train That Goes Through a Building

location.name: Liziba Monorail Viewing Platform 李子坝轻轨观景台, Yuzhong District

references.title: Multiple viewing spots for the shot

tiktoks.script:
## Getting there

**The viewing platform is outside the turnstiles.** Free, at street level, no metro ticket — the obvious move of going into the station to find the train is the wrong one. Come out at **Exit 2** and follow the signs to 观景台. Exit 1 works too but loops the long way round.

## Angles

- **The platform opposite** — the classic frame. Built at a deliberate 33° to the building for exactly this shot.
- **Inside the station and the corridors** — then ride one stop for the in-motion version.
- **Sixth-floor reading room** — floor-to-ceiling windows straight onto the track, air conditioned. You have to buy something; water counts.
- **Lansheng Pavilion**, 370m away, 10–15 min of climbing — gets the train, the tower and the Jialing River in one frame.

## Timing

- Trains every 3–8 min, ~6:30–23:00. Tightest at 07:30–09:30 and 17:00–19:00.
- Light and crowds don't peak together: the crush is 12:00–15:00, the good light is 14:00–17:00. **From about 15:00** gets you both.
- Emptiest is 07:00–09:00 — by 08:00 on a weekday, 08:30 at the weekend.
- Budget 20–30 min for 3–4 passes.

## Open questions

- Which of these the reel actually uses, and whether it has a spot I haven't got here
- Whether the Lansheng Pavilion climb is worth it for a vertical crop, or whether it only reads wide
- Whether a tripod is tolerated on the platform when it's busy

tiktoks.title: The Cable Car Inside a Mall

location.name: Super Wenheyou 超级文和友, 36 Xiangjiang Middle Road, Tianxin District

references.title: Super Wenheyou — floors, hours and the cable car

tiktoks.script:
## Getting there

**Super Wenheyou 超级文和友** — floors 1–6 of Hisense Plaza 海信广场, at the address you gave. Metro: Xiangjiang Middle Road Station, Line 2 Exit 3, 3–5 min walk. Huangxing Square on Line 1 also works.

## The cable car

**Fifth floor.** The sign in the photo reads 文和友缆车售票处 ← 五楼 — "Wenheyou cable car ticket office, 5th floor". Around ¥20 a person to ride it.

## Practical

- Open 11:00–02:00.
- **Free to walk in and film.** The queue everyone warns about is for *food*, not entry — 2h+ on evenings and weekends, run through an online number system. You can ignore all of it if you're only shooting.
- Quietest 14:00–17:00, or before 17:00 on a weekday.
- The cable car is one prop inside a much bigger set: the whole venue is a recreated 1980s Changsha street stacked six floors high. Worth budgeting time for the building itself.

## Open questions

- Whether you can film from inside the car while it's moving, or only from the walkways
- Whether the ¥20 ride uses the same number-taking system as the restaurants
- Whether the cable car runs the full 11:00–02:00 or shorter hours than the venue

tiktoks.title: The Taxi With Nobody in the Front Seat

location.name: Qianhai 前海, Nanshan District

references.title: Robotaxi for foreign tourists — what actually works in 2026
Shenzhen operators, zones and hours

tiktoks.script:
## Booking it is the hard part

Every robotaxi app needs a **+86 number** for SMS verification — get a passport-registered Chinese SIM at the airport.

Then the catch: **Apollo Go 萝卜快跑 — the operator in the photo, it's printed on the steering wheel cover — typically wants a Chinese ID at signup**, and as of 2026 still mostly blocks foreign IDs. Solo registration may simply fail.

Routes, most to least likely to work:

1. **Pony.ai 小马智行** — holds Shenzhen's first citywide fully-driverless commercial permit, 1,000+ L4 cars. PonyPilot+ app (小马智行), its WeChat mini-program, or through Gaode Maps.
2. **Tencent's Futian pilot** — small coverage, but reportedly the one with explicit foreign-traveller access. WeChat mini-program.
3. **Apollo Go** — Baidu Maps app, or the 萝卜快跑 mini-program. Worth a try; don't build the day around it.
4. Failing all of it: a local books, you ride.

## Where

Not a venue, a service zone.

- **Pony.ai** — Qianhai 前海 and parts of Nanshan / Bao'an. 08:30–22:30.
- **Apollo Go** — Pingshan, Nanshan, parts of Bao'an. 07:00–23:00.
- Three passengers max.

## Open questions

- Whether a passport alone clears Pony.ai signup in Shenzhen, or whether that wants a Chinese ID too
- Door-to-door or fixed pickup points — no source I found committed either way
- What a ride costs and how long you wait
- Whether the empty driver's seat reads on camera without a wide lens, or whether the shot is really the wheel turning by itself

## What it is

**Orbit One 奥彼文星球食研所** — space-themed, and the gimmick is the delivery. Dishes ride UFO-shaped carriers along a **magnetic levitation track mounted on the ceiling**, stop above your table and descend onto it. Holographic galaxy tables, planet lamps, the lot.

- Metro Line 6, **Science Museum Station 科学馆站**. Sources disagree on the exit — one says Exit E (~260m), another Exit F (~490m). Either way you're in the right mall.
- Mon–Thu and Sun 11:30–21:00. Fri–Sat 11:30–21:30.
- Around ¥99 a head.

## Open questions

tiktoks.title: DJI Sky City

location.name: DJI Sky City 大疆天空之城, 55 Xianyuan Road, Nanshan District

references.title: Reel — DJI Sky City and the Civic Center

tiktoks.script:
## What it is

DJI's global headquarters, in Liuxiandong, Xili, Nanshan. **Foster + Partners**, finished December 2022. Two towers — roughly **213m and 195m** — joined by an **open-air suspension bridge 100m up**. The floors are hung from steel cores, which is why the stacked volumes appear to float clear of each other; that's the thing the night lighting picks out.

## Access — read this before you plan a day around it

It's a **working corporate campus** for ~8,000 staff. I found no confirmed visitor centre, observation deck or public interior. Treat this as an **exterior shoot** until proven otherwise.

The DJI **flagship store is somewhere else entirely** — OCT Harbour, Baishi Road, Nanshan (10:00–22:00, later Fri/Sat). That's the one that's open to the public, if you want hands-on product as a second scene.

## Open questions

- Whether you can get onto the plaza at the base or only shoot from the street
- Whether security move you on for filming, especially with a tripod or a drone
- Where the angle in the reel is actually shot from
- Whether the facade lighting runs nightly or only at set times

tiktoks.title: The Civic Center Light Show

location.name: Civic Center Square 市民广场, Futian District

references.title: Reel — DJI Sky City and the Civic Center

tiktoks.script:
## The catch: the square needs a booking

Watching from **Civic Center Square itself requires a free reservation**, through the 福田中心区夜景灯光预约导引服务 WeChat mini-program. Turning up without one is the way this goes wrong.

**No booking is needed from nearby vantage points** — Lianhua Hill 莲花山 is the usual one, about a 10-minute climb, and it's the better frame anyway: the whole CBD skyline with Ping An behind it rather than the towers looming over you.

So: book if you want the square and the LED floor tiles in shot. Skip the booking and climb the hill if you want the skyline.

## When

- **Fridays and Saturdays**, plus the day before and during Chinese public holidays — New Year, Spring Festival, Labour Day, Dragon Boat, Mid-Autumn, National Day.
- **Nov–Mar:** 19:00, 20:00, 21:00. **Apr–Oct:** 19:30, 20:30, 21:30.
- Each show runs **15 minutes**.
- Metro Line 2 or 4 to Civic Center Station, Exit B or F.

## Shooting notes

- Record video, not stills — the animation is the point.
- Tripod worth having; it's a long, dark, wide subject.
- Best reflections come right after rain, off the square.
- For the square, get there well before the show to hold a spot.

## Open questions

- Whether the reservation is bookable by a foreign passport / non-Chinese WeChat, or needs a local
- How far ahead the slots go and whether they sell out
- Which of the three nightly shows is least crowded

tiktoks.title: The White House Copy

location.name: Huaguoyuan White House 花果园白宫, 99 Huaguoyuan Street, Nanming District

references.title: Guiyang White House — access, viewing angles, getting there

tiktoks.script:
## Exterior only

**No public entry.** Routine access to the main building isn't permitted and staff patrol the perimeter. The ground floor occasionally hosts exhibitions, but it isn't a visitor venue. The facade and the reflecting pond *are* the attraction — free, no ticket.

Officially it's the **Boyang Art International Exchange Center 博样艺术国际交流中心**; everyone calls it 花果园白宫, the Huaguoyuan White House. Roughly 12 storeys, reportedly ¥2.7bn to build, and the landmark of the Huaguoyuan district.

Worth noting for the script: it doesn't look much like the actual White House up close — it's closer to a vast French château with Roman columns and domes. The nickname does a lot of work.

## Where and when

- 99 Huaguoyuan Street, Nanming District — Songhua South Road, opposite Huaguoyuan Wetland Park and the Huaguoyuan Shopping Center.
- **Huaguoyuan metro station**, 5–10 min walk. Taxi from Guiyang railway station 15–25 min, from the airport 40–60 min.
- **Late afternoon into the first hour after sunset** is the light.

## Angles

- **Across the pond** — the reflection shot, the signature one.
- **The eastern walkway** — shows how deep the building actually goes.
- The photo here is from above, so somebody is getting an elevated angle — worth finding what building or hillside that's from.

## Open questions

- Where that aerial-ish angle is shot from, and whether it's a public vantage point
- Whether drones are tolerated here, given the perimeter patrols
- Whether the ground-floor exhibitions run on any predictable schedule
- Whether Guiyang is worth a fourth city for one building, or whether it pairs with something else in Guizhou

tiktoks.title: Qianchun Interchange

location.name: Qianchun Interchange 黔春立交, Beijing West Road, Yunyan District

references.title: Aerial view and the numbers behind it

tiktoks.script:
## The numbers

**Five levels, 11 ramps, 8 entrances and exits, and a 55m vertical drop** between top and bottom. Opened 2017 after eight-plus years of design and construction. Routinely called the most complex interchange in China.

It sits on Beijing West Road in Yunyan District, between the Qianchun and Haimahong tunnels, linking Huaguoyuan with Guanshanhu.

## The problem: it only reads from the air

Every shot that made this famous — including the one on this card — is aerial. From the ground it's just an underpass; the five stacked levels and the whole roller-coaster geometry disappear. **That's the thing to solve before committing to it.**

Options, in order of how likely they are to work:

1. **A high floor with a line of sight** — Guiyang is hilly and dense, so there may be a tower or hillside overlooking it. Worth scouting on a map before going.
2. **A drone.** Which is the honest answer for what's on this card, and also the part with the most unknowns — see below.
3. **From inside a car**, driving the ramps. A different video, but a real one: five levels, 55m of drop, and the drive itself is the story.

## Pairs with the White House

Both are in Guiyang and the interchange connects to **Huaguoyuan** — the same district as [the White House copy]. Two subjects in one city changes the maths on whether Guiyang is worth the detour.

## Open questions

- Whether flying a drone here is permitted, what registration a foreign visitor needs, and whether this counts as restricted airspace. **Resolve this before planning around the aerial shot.**
- Whether any public building or hillside gives an elevated line of sight
- Whether the night lighting runs all evening
- Whether the in-car version is actually interesting or just a tunnel

tiktoks.title: Panda Valley

location.name: Panda Valley 熊猫谷, Yutang Town, Dujiangyan

references.title: The TikTok — has more references in it
Panda Valley vs the other bases — booking, transport, timings

tiktoks.script:
## Book before you go — there is no ticket window

**¥55, advance booking only**, through WeChat or the official site. No walk-up. This is the one that would waste a whole morning.

## Which panda place this actually is

Three sites get muddled constantly, so:

- **Panda Valley 熊猫谷** — this one. The Chengdu base's field station, 134 hectares of forested hillside in Yutang Town, ~3km outside Dujiangyan. Naturalistic open enclosures and a free-roaming red panda path. Quiet.
- **Chengdu Panda Base** (city) — the famous one, Hua Hua, tens of thousands of visitors a day. Closer to a theme park than a reserve.
- **Dujiangyan Panda Base** — a *different* facility again, and **temporarily closed for renovation since 23 April 2026**. Don't let a search result send you there.

The reason to pick this one for a video is exactly the reason it's less famous: woodland, few people, pandas at a distance you can actually frame. The photo is bamboo and leaf litter, not concrete.

## Getting there and when

- Metro Line 6 to **Xibu Station** → intercity train to **Liduiyuan Station** (~40 min, ¥10) → Bus 14 or a short taxi. Or DiDi door-to-door, 60–80 min, ¥120–180.
- **Active window is roughly 08:30–10:30.** Sources disagree on exactly when keepers arrive — one says 08:30, another 09:30 — but they agree the morning is when the pandas move. Be there for opening.
- Hours: 07:30–18:00 from 16 Mar to 31 Oct, 08:00–17:30 otherwise.
- Allow 2–4 hours.

## Open questions

- **What else the TikTok recommends** — it's JS-rendered so I couldn't read it. Worth watching it yourself and pulling the other spots out into their own entries.
- Whether the booking works on a foreign passport and a non-Chinese WeChat, or needs a local
- How far ahead slots go and whether they sell out
- Whether tripods are allowed, and how close the enclosures actually let you get

tiktoks.title: Chengdu Twin Towers

location.name: Jiaozi Ring Bridge 交子之环, Jiaozi Financial District

references.title: Light show schedule and the best viewpoints

tiktoks.script:
## Free, nightly, no booking

Unlike the Shenzhen Civic Center show, this one needs **no reservation and costs nothing**. It runs **every night, 19:30–22:00**, and the themed scenes change roughly every half hour — so if you miss one, wait ten minutes.

## Where to stand

The location on this card is the **viewing spot, not the towers** — same logic as Liziba.

- **Jiaozi Ring Bridge 交子之环** — the futuristic orange pedestrian loop. Unobstructed, front-row, dead-on view of both facades. **Be there by 19:20** for a place at the railing; it fills up on holidays.
- **Jiaozi Park** — 10 minutes' walk, and the lake gives you the reflection version. Quieter.
- **SKP entrance plaza** — the third usual angle.

## Timing

- **Blue hour is the shot.** About half an hour after sunset, the sky still deep blue against the LEDs — far better than full black.
- If you miss it, **20:00–21:00** is when the sky is dark enough for the LEDs to punch.
- Arrive ~10 min before a scene change.

## Open questions

- Whether the ring bridge is wide enough to set up a tripod without blocking people
- Whether the content rotates nightly or repeats the same scenes
- Whether the park reflection needs still water, i.e. a windless evening
- Whether the towers themselves have any public observation level

tiktoks.title: Du Fu Thatched Cottage

location.name: Du Fu Thatched Cottage 杜甫草堂, 37 Qinghua Road, Qingyang District

references.title: Hours, ticket, metro and what to see inside

tiktoks.script:
## Shoot it in the rain

The photo on this card is wet flagstones, dripping eaves and lit lanterns — and that is the version worth having. Grey and raining is the look here, not blue sky. Chengdu obliges more often than not.

## Practical

- **Metro Line 4 to Caotang Road North 草堂北路站**, then ~15 min / 1km walk. 37 Qinghua Road, Qingyang District.
- **Hours** 08:00–20:00 in summer, 08:00–18:30 in winter — sources put the changeover at either end of October. Ticket office shuts an hour before the gate.
- **¥50–60** depending on which source you believe.
- Allow **2.5–3 hours** for the whole site; far less if you're only after two or three shots.

## What's actually photogenic

- **The Flower Path 花径** — the corridor of red walls with bamboo shadows thrown across them. This is the shot the place is known for.
- **Bamboo groves** through the gardens.
- **The thatched hut replica**, with the little bridge over the stream.

Best months are March–April for blossom and September–October for clear air.

## Open questions

- Whether the red-wall corridor gets queues for photos, and how early you'd need to be
- Whether tripods are allowed inside
- Whether it's worth pairing with anything nearby to justify the trip out west

tiktoks.title: Bar 93

location.name: Bar 93, Niccolo Changsha, Tower 1, Changsha IFS, 188 Jiefang West Road, Furong District

references.title: Niccolo Changsha — the hotel
Bar 93 — hours, booking, contact

tiktoks.script:
## What and where

**Bar 93** — the 93rd floor of Niccolo Changsha, in **IFS Tower 1**, 188 Jiefang West Road. The name is literal: it's the floor. Billed as the highest bar in Changsha.

The photo is the hotel's own promotional shot, so the actual light and crowd will differ — but the window-wall river view is real and roughly what you'd get at a window table around dusk.

- **Book ahead** — there's an online reservation system, worth using rather than walking in.
- Cocktails and a DJ/live-performer program in the evenings — this reads as a bar with a view, not primarily a dinner spot, worth knowing if the plan is food.

tiktoks.title: Walking Nanming District

location.name: Huaguoyuan 花果园, Nanming District

references.title: Nanming District — attractions, streets, food

tiktoks.script:
## Your photo is Huaguoyuan

The cover is a labelled aerial of **Huaguoyuan 花果园** — the exact neighbourhood the White House copy and the Qianchun Interchange are already in. So this entry isn't a new area, it's the connective tissue between the two: a walking/exploring piece for the district they both sit in, plus what else is worth wandering into.

Huaguoyuan itself is one of the densest urban complexes in China — ~400,000 people, and it's Guiyang's de facto new city centre. **Huaguoyuan Night Market** is the specific thing to walk into: trendy, young crowd, dense eateries packed around it.

## Elsewhere in Nanming, south of the river

- **Qingyun Road Night Fair** — Wang's Dessert, lobster, bake pot, fresh dumplings.
- **Erqi Road food street.**
- **Jiaxiu Tower** and **Qingyun Market**, both south of the Nanming River — more classical/old-town in character than Huaguoyuan's high-rise density.
- **Huaguoyuan Wetland Park** for a quieter walk if the market gets to be too much.

## The shape of the piece

This reads as a between-shots wander rather than a single subject — walk from the White House, through Huaguoyuan's night market, and either stop there or push on to Qingyun Road for the older, food-street version of Guiyang. Two very different textures in one day if you want the contrast.

## Open questions

- Whether Qingyun Road is walkable from Huaguoyuan or needs its own trip
- Best night for the market — whether it's every night or weekends only
- Whether daytime Huaguoyuan (the density, the architecture) is worth its own separate walk from the night market energy

tiktoks.title: Future Ark

location.name: 未来方舟 Future Ark, Yunyan District

references.title: [4K] Walk through the hillside residential towers
Design concept and the 380m landmark tower

tiktoks.script:
## What it is

**未来方舟, Zhongtian Future Ark**, Yunyan District — built into a hillside between the mountains and the Nanming River. The terraced residential towers step down from the foothills to the riverfront, deliberately echoing the way villages stack up mountainsides in Guizhou. That's the "vertical residential system" — it's not a metaphor, the buildings are literally terraced with the slope.

## Two different things share the name — check which one you mean

- **The residential hillside city** — the part in your photo, and what the walkthrough video shows. Built, lived-in, walkable.
- **The Future Ark WTC / landmark tower** — a separate 380m tower with office, hotel and mall space, described as still under construction. Don't expect to get inside this part yet.

## Getting the shot

There's a confirmed **YouTube walkthrough filmed at street level among the towers** — worth watching before you go, since it's the closest thing to a scouted route I found. Your own photo is shot from a roadside footpath with a railing, looking across at the towers lit up at night — that's a real, repeatable vantage point, not an aerial.

## Open questions

- Exact name/location of the road your photo was taken from
- Whether the WTC tower construction site is visible/interesting from the same spot, or a separate detour
- Daytime vs night — the photo is a night shot and the towers are clearly lit for it; whether daytime shows the terracing better

tiktoks.title: Rooftop Coffee on the 30th Floor

location.name: 屋顶咖啡（亨特店）, 文昌第居 20栋1单元 3004, 文昌南路, 南明区

references.title: Ctrip listing — hours, price, the 270° view

tiktoks.script:
## Why this is the hook, not just a nice café

It's on the **30th floor of an ordinary residential building** — Wenchang Diju 文昌第居, Building 20, Unit 1. You go up in a normal residential lift, and it opens onto a full rooftop terrace and a two-storey structure that used to be a **Qiandongnan intangible-heritage museum**. Nothing on the street or the building's exterior suggests any of this is up there. That's the whole video: ordinary tower block in, rooftop world out.

## Exact address, room and how to actually get there

**贵阳市南明区文昌南路文昌第居20栋1单元30层5号** — room **3004**.

Navigation, precisely: go to **Hunter International Plaza 亨特国际广场** on Wenchang South Road. Find **山荀料理** (Shanxun Japanese cuisine) — the entrance is the **lift behind/next to it**, not a street-facing door. One version of the directions has you entering from the right side of the underground garage, next to the Japanese restaurant opposite Hunter International, then up to 30F. Take that lift to the 30th floor and look for **3004 / 屋顶咖啡**.

**District labelling is genuinely inconsistent** — some coffee guides file it under Yunyan 云岩区, but the address itself, and Wenchang Diju as a building, sit in Nanming 南明区. The building/room is the reliable part; the district name isn't.

## What's actually up there (Ctrip listing)

- **270° panoramic view**, floor-to-ceiling windows.
- Two floors: an artistic indoor space below, an independent private room above.
- **10:00–22:00**, roughly **¥40–60 a head**.
- Long-running and still busy — not a pop-up.

## Open questions

- Whether the lift is accessible to non-residents without a resident buzzing you up
- Whether the terrace shot needs a booking, or you can just turn up
- Best light — the photo is dusk, worth checking if daytime changes the view much

tiktoks.title: Haitangxi Tongzilou

location.name: 海棠溪筒子楼 (Haitangxi Tongzilou), 海棠溪正街31–32号, 南岸区

references.title: Independent write-up — 1999, 13 floors, the Better Days connection

tiktoks.script:
## What it actually is

Not abandoned. A **real, occupied residential building** from 1999, 13 floors, roughly 8 households per floor, no lift — Z-shaped stairs wrap an enormous open central atrium the full height of the building. That atrium and the repeating diagonal stair lines are what make it read as a megastructure rather than an apartment block.

## Why it's known

It's Chen Nian 陈念's home in the 2019 film **《少年的你》— Better Days**, shot in Chongqing in 2018. That's most of why it went viral as a photography spot. The reveal order is the whole pitch: ordinary building from outside → walk in → the atrium → discover it's someone's actual home → find out it was in a film.

It also sits right beside the Sheraton Chongqing twin towers — old 1990s Tongzilou next to glass-and-glow modern Chongqing, in the same frame if you shoot the exterior wide.

## Exact location

**海棠溪筒子楼**, 重庆市南岸区海棠溪街道海棠溪正街 31–32号. Government sources point at 31号 specifically; map/travel listings usually give 31–32号 together. Chinese text to show a driver or paste into Amap/DiDi: **海棠溪筒子楼** or **重庆市南岸区海棠溪正街31-32号**.

**Two entrances, and they're not equivalent** — a travel guide reports that 32号 reaches the bottom of the atrium and 31号 doesn't. For the straight-up-from-the-bottom hero shot, try **32号** first.

## It is someone's home — read this before you go

Not a ruin, not a set. Residents live here, and the building has become popular enough that Nan'an authorities have documented residents moving toward self-managed visitor/filming arrangements — including a reported ¥200 filming fee charged to a production crew in 2023. Casual photography has historically been tolerated; a visible film crew is a different thing.

- Keep the kit small — camera, one lens, a mic, at most a monopod. Not a full rig.
- Don't block stairways or corridors.
- Ask before filming anyone directly; never shoot into apartment windows.
- If someone tells you to stop or asks for a fee, comply rather than argue.
- No drone — pointless inside, and the area around it is dense low-rise anyway.

## Recreating the reference shot

The photo here is the shot to aim for: centred structural column, repeating diagonal stairs, a single small person for scale. Go as low as possible in the atrium, shoot straight across rather than on a diagonal, keep the central column dead centre. Widest lens available. A light/white shirt on the person separates them from the dark structure — dark clothing disappears into it.

## A shot list, roughly in order

1. Exterior on 海棠溪正街 — establish it as an unremarkable old building.
2. Walk in, footsteps, then the reveal as the atrium opens up.
3. Bottom of the atrium, tilt slowly up all 13 floors.
4. Wide static shot, person walks through for scale.
5. Follow someone up the Z-stairs — footsteps, railings, doors, distant voices.
6. A few floors up, looking back down.
7. Exterior again, this time compressed against the Sheraton towers with a longer lens.

Sound is worth dedicating time to on its own: 5–10 minutes of clean atrium ambience — footsteps, stair creaks, doors, distant conversation, wind through the shaft. The location is unusually good for this.

## Timing

Two real options, both defensible:
- **16:30 onward** — exterior in good light, then the atrium gets progressively darker and moodier as you go, genuinely atmospheric by evening.
- **Overcast midday** — one report describes the atrium going grey and almost filmic on cloudy days, versus hard light shafts when it's sunny. Overcast suits a darker cinematic look better than direct sun.

## Getting there

Haitangxi rail station, then to 海棠溪正街31号 on foot, or DiDi straight to the address — parking nearby is reportedly difficult, so don't drive yourself.

## Open questions

- Whether 32号's access to the bottom still holds — worth confirming on arrival rather than assuming
- Current asking price if a resident does raise a filming fee
- Whether the stairs need a phone light on the darker sections, as one visitor reported

tiktoks.title: Xicun Courtyard

location.name: 西村大院 (Xicun Courtyard / West Village), 贝森北路1号, 青羊区

references.title: People's Daily — the track, the sports facilities, Liu Jiakun

tiktoks.script:
## What it is

Not a shopping complex — a five-storey building wrapped around a sports courtyard, and the "roof" is a **1.6km elevated running/walking track** that spirals up from ground level to the fifth-floor rooftop. Inside the perimeter: a football pitch, basketball courts, gardens, shops and cafés, all wrapped by that one continuous track.

Designed by **Liu Jiakun**, 2025 Pritzker Prize. Completed 2014–15 (sources give both years).

## The shot

This one needs the reveal structure, not a wide establishing shot:

1. Outside — it reads as an ordinary, slightly odd complex.
2. Walk in.
3. Keep walking upward, following the track.
4. You're now looking down at Chengdu from what appears to be a street on the roof of a building.

Hook options: *"There is a public street running around the roof of this building in Chengdu"* or *"I thought I was walking around the ground floor… until I looked down."*

## Practical

- 西村大院, 成都市青羊区贝森北路1号.
- Metro **文化宫站, Lines 4 & 7**.
- **Free.** Hours given as 10:00–22:00.
- **16:30–20:30** — the sports fields read best around sunset.

## What I could and couldn't confirm

Independently verified: the 1.6km spiralling track, the football pitch and basketball court, the Liu Jiakun/Pritzker credit. Couldn't independently confirm the exact address, hours or metro line from a second source — they're taken as supplied.

## Open questions

- Whether the whole 1.6km loop is open to walk at all hours, or just during the 10:00–22:00 window
- Whether the sports fields are ever in active use and off-limits to bystanders
- Best point to start the ascent for the cleanest reveal shot

**MO Bar**, 79th floor of the **Mandarin Oriental Shenzhen** — Block A, UpperHills, 5001 Huanggang Road, Futian. Ranked **#5 on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026**.

Your photo is the corner window seats — floor-to-ceiling glass, Ping An Finance Centre visible in the skyline. That specific seating is the thing to know about:

## The seats in your photo are not bookable

**Limited window seats are walk-in only** — not available for reservation. A select number of other seats can be reserved subject to availability, and reservations go through the hotel directly (+86 755 8182 9379). So getting the shot in your reference photo means turning up and hoping, not booking ahead.

## Practical

- **18:00–01:00 Sun–Thu, 18:00–02:00 Fri–Sat.**
- **18+ only.**
- New cocktail menu as of early 2025, per one write-up — worth checking what's current when you go.
